sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·荣森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之爱及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我那个黑胶唱片时代的夜店当DJ的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每晚都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Russia's military failures have defined its war against Ukraine and were exemplified by a major attack this week in which dozens of Russian soldiers were killed as they slept in their barracks.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯的军事失利定义了其对乌克兰的战争，本周发生的一起重大袭击事件就是例证，数十名俄罗斯士兵在军营睡觉时被炸死。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Michael Schwartz interviews Russian soldiers and reveals new details about how this military superpower keeps making the same mistakes and why,
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事迈克尔·施瓦茨采访了俄罗斯士兵，揭示了关于这个军事超级大国为何不断重蹈覆辙的新细节，以及为什么，

sentences.en: despite all of that, its soldiers keep going back to fight.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，它的士兵们还是不断地回去参战。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, January 4th.
sentences.zh: 今天是1月4日，星期三。

sentences.en: So, Mike, you have been investigating this question I think a lot of us have had, those of us who've been paying attention to the war in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 那么，迈克，你一直在调查这个问题，我想我们很多人，那些一直关注乌克兰战争的人，都有过这个疑问。

sentences.en: And that is this, that both Russia and I think to a certain extent the world thought that Russia would just roll in and defeat the Ukrainians outright, right?
sentences.zh: 那就是，俄罗斯，我想在某种程度上全世界也认为，俄罗斯会直接长驱直入并彻底击败乌克兰人，对吧？

sentences.en: Like they'd roll into the capital, take it in three days, the war would be over.
sentences.zh: 就像他们会开进首都，三天内拿下，战争就结束了。

sentences.en: But that obviously didn't happen, like not even close.
sentences.zh: 但显然这并没有发生，甚至差得远呢。

sentences.en: So, you and our colleagues decided to take a deep look into how the Russian forces failed so badly.
sentences.zh: 所以，你和我们的同事决定深入研究俄罗斯军队为何失败得如此惨烈。

sentences.en: So, tell me what you guys did.
sentences.zh: 那么，告诉我你们做了些什么。

sentences.en: What my colleagues and I decided to do is really drill down into the question of why.
sentences.zh: 我和同事们决定深入探讨“为什么”这个问题。

sentences.en: Why is it that this military that the entire world thought was advanced, was huge, was deadly, was menacing,
sentences.zh: 为什么这支全世界都认为先进、庞大、致命、具有威胁性的军队，

sentences.en: how were they unable to carry out the war plans that everybody envisioned, that the Russians envisioned, that the West envisioned?
sentences.zh: 竟然无法执行每个人预想中、俄罗斯人预想中、西方预想中的战争计划？

sentences.en: And one of the important questions I wanted to answer was how the Russians themselves viewed this war,
sentences.zh: 我想要回答的一个重要问题是，俄罗斯人自己是如何看待这场战争的，

sentences.en: what they thought of what they were doing, and what they thought of their success, how they evaluated their performance.
sentences.zh: 他们对自己所做的事情有何想法，对自己的成功有何看法，以及他们如何评估自己的表现。

sentences.en: And so, we really worked hard to try and find copies of Russian correspondence, diaries, call logs, battle plans.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们确实努力寻找了俄罗斯的通信记录、日记、通话记录和作战计划的副本。

sentences.en: And we went around and interviewed as many Russian soldiers as we could find as well.
sentences.zh: 我们也到处采访了我们能找到的尽可能多的俄罗斯士兵。

sentences.en: This was in POW camps.
sentences.zh: 这包括在战俘营里进行的采访。

sentences.en: This was by phone, Russians that we could connect to, who had been on the battlefield, who had returned to Russia.
sentences.zh: 也通过电话采访了那些我们能联系上的、曾上过战场并已回到俄罗斯的俄罗斯人。

sentences.en: So, tell me what you guys found.
sentences.zh: 那么，告诉我你们发现了什么。

sentences.en: Where should we start?
sentences.zh: 我们该从哪里开始呢？

sentences.en: Well, we can start at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们可以从头说起。

sentences.en: And the thing that everybody needs to understand is just how overconfident the Russians were.
sentences.zh: 每个人都需要明白的一点是，俄罗斯人当时是多么的自负。

sentences.en: They planned to take Ukraine and topple the government in Kiev, the capital.
sentences.zh: 他们计划占领乌克兰并推翻首都基辅的政府。

sentences.en: Troops were going to race in from three directions, seize the government, and that would be the end of the war.
sentences.zh: 部队将从三个方向冲入，夺取政权，战争就此结束。

sentences.en: But when we started speaking to Russian soldiers, we realized that they didn't have any idea what that plan was.
sentences.zh: 但当我们开始与俄罗斯士兵交谈时，我们意识到他们根本不知道那个计划是什么。

sentences.en: Many of them didn't find out about it until the hours before the war began.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人直到战争开始前几个小时才知道。

sentences.en: I spoke to a corporal named Nikita Chybrin.
sentences.zh: 我采访了一位名叫尼基塔·奇布林的下士。

sentences.en: He's a 27-year-old soldier in a motorized infantry brigade.
sentences.zh: 他是一名27岁的摩托化步兵旅士兵。

sentences.en: And he said he spent a month before the war in Belarus, which is the country north of Ukraine, on what he and his fellow soldiers were told was a training exercise,
sentences.zh: 他说他在战前在白俄罗斯（乌克兰北部的国家）待了一个月，他和战友们被告知是在进行军事演习，

sentences.en: but what he described as more like camping.
sentences.zh: 但他形容那更像是露营。

sentences.en: There was no military exercises involved.
sentences.zh: 根本没有任何军事演习。

sentences.en: And on February 23rd, the day before the invasion was announced, he and his unit were in their camp celebrating Defender of the Fatherland holiday,
sentences.zh: 2月23日，即宣布入侵的前一天，他和他的部队在营地庆祝“祖国保卫者日”，

sentences.en: which is a Russian national holiday for service members.
sentences.zh: 这是一个俄罗斯军人的全国性节日。

sentences.en: And they were snacking on candy for the occasion when their commander approached.
sentences.zh: 他们当时正在吃糖果庆祝，这时指挥官走了过来。

sentences.en: And the commander told them only, and I'm quoting, tomorrow you are going to Ukraine to fuck up some shit.
sentences.zh: 指挥官只对他们说了这样一句话，我引用原话：“明天你们要去乌克兰搞点破坏。”

sentences.en: And beyond that, they were given no further orders.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，他们没有接到任何进一步的命令。

sentences.en: Another soldier that we interviewed, who was stationed in Belarus, said he found out he was going to war only an hour before his unit began to march.
sentences.zh: 我们采访的另一名驻扎在白俄罗斯的士兵说，他直到部队开始行军前一小时才知道自己要去打仗。

sentences.en: And the only order that he was given was that he was supposed to just drive straight and follow the vehicle in front of him with no explanation beyond that.
sentences.zh: 他接到的唯一命令就是一直往前开，跟着前面的车，没有给出任何解释。

sentences.en: God, it's amazing.
sentences.zh: 天哪，这太不可思议了。

sentences.en: It's amazing that they knew so little and were so ill-prepared.
sentences.zh: 他们知道的这么少，准备得这么不充分，真是令人震惊。

sentences.en: And to your point, they were just so overconfident.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，他们实在是太自负了。

sentences.en: They thought it would be a cakewalk.
sentences.zh: 他们以为这会是一场轻松的胜利。

sentences.en: But instead of the war being over quickly, it just started to drag on.
sentences.zh: 但战争并没有迅速结束，反而开始陷入僵局。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this was devastating, particularly for the Russian troops on the ground in that first push into Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 这对在第一波攻势中进入乌克兰的俄军来说是毁灭性的。

sentences.en: Very quickly, they came under incredibly heavy fire from Ukrainian troops that were in smaller units, in more nimble units.
sentences.zh: 很快，他们就遭到了乌克兰军队极其猛烈的炮火攻击，乌军的单位更小、更灵活。

sentences.en: And not only are a lot of soldiers dying, but a lot of Russia's most elite troops.
sentences.zh: 不仅大量士兵阵亡，而且很多是俄罗斯最精锐的部队。

sentences.en: These are the special forces units.
sentences.zh: 这些是特种部队单位。

sentences.en: These are the airborne units.
sentences.zh: 这些是空降部队单位。

sentences.en: And hundreds and hundreds were killed.
sentences.zh: 成百上千人被杀。

sentences.en: OK, so the Russians right out of the gate lost a lot of their highly trained guys.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以俄罗斯人一开战就损失了大量训练有素的人员。

sentences.en: And that was a huge problem for them.
sentences.zh: 这对他们来说是个大问题。

sentences.en: So how did they deal with it?
sentences.zh: 那么他们是如何应对的呢？

sentences.en: Like, how did the Russian military see a way out of that fix they were in?
sentences.zh: 也就是说，俄罗斯军方是如何看待摆脱困境的方法的？

sentences.en: Well, the first thing they did is pull all of their troops out of northern Ukraine and away from Kiev.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们做的第一件事就是把所有部队从乌克兰北部撤出，远离基辅。

sentences.en: The plan was to reconsolidate them in the east and the south and reconstitute some of these units that had been decimated.
sentences.zh: 计划是在东部和南部重新集结，并重建一些被摧毁的部队。

sentences.en: But what they really needed was more guys.
sentences.zh: 但他们真正需要的是更多的人手。

sentences.en: So the Kremlin and the military started trying to find ways to bulk up their forces with more men.
sentences.zh: 于是克里姆林宫和军方开始想办法用更多的人来扩充兵力。

sentences.en: One of the things they did was turn to a mercenary group called Wagner that had experience all over the Middle East and Africa.
sentences.zh: 他们采取的措施之一是求助于一个名为“瓦格纳”的雇佣兵组织，该组织在中东和非洲各地都有经验。

sentences.en: And these are highly trained soldiers.
sentences.zh: 这些都是训练有素的士兵。

sentences.en: So, in other words, because Russia unexpectedly loses all of their experienced guys, in a sort of desperate move, they turn to this group of hired guns, the Wagner group.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，因为俄罗斯意外损失了所有经验丰富的士兵，在一种绝望的举动下，他们转向了这群雇佣兵，即瓦格纳集团。

sentences.en: Remind us who they are.
sentences.zh: 提醒我们一下他们是谁。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: This is a group that got started coming on a decade ago, and it has the appearance of a military contractor.
sentences.zh: 这是一个大约十年前开始出现的组织，看起来像是一家军事承包商。

sentences.en: It was started by this man by the name of Yevgeny Prigozhin.
sentences.zh: 它是由一个名叫叶夫根尼·普里戈任的人创办的。

sentences.en: This is a businessman who has catered Kremlin events in the past, and so he's a connection to Vladimir Putin.
sentences.zh: 这是一位过去曾为克里姆林宫活动提供餐饮服务的商人，所以他和弗拉基米尔·普京有联系。

sentences.en: A caterer.
sentences.zh: 一个餐饮承办商？

sentences.en: He's a caterer and a businessman.
sentences.zh: 他既是餐饮承办商也是商人。

sentences.en: He has had very large contracts catering the military, catering Russian schools, and he has been photographed serving Vladimir Putin food at different state functions.
sentences.zh: 他曾获得过非常大的合同，为军队和俄罗斯学校提供餐饮，并且在不同的国家职能部门中被拍到为弗拉基米尔·普京上菜。

sentences.en: And, Mike, why would a caterer run a militia?
sentences.zh: 那么，迈克，为什么一个餐饮承办商会经营一支民兵组织？

sentences.en: That's one of the mysteries of the Wagner group, how he got into running a militia.
sentences.zh: 这是瓦格纳集团的谜团之一，他是如何开始经营民兵组织的。

sentences.en: It is only in the last few months that Prigozhin has taken responsibility for founding the Wagner group.
sentences.zh: 直到最近几个月，普里戈任才承认自己是瓦格纳集团的创始人。

sentences.en: In the past, he's denied even its existence and sued journalists who have alleged that he is behind it.
sentences.zh: 过去，他甚至否认其存在，并起诉那些指控他是幕后黑手的记者。

sentences.en: Oh, interesting.
sentences.zh: 哦，有意思。

sentences.en: So it was like a secret thing.
sentences.zh: 所以这就像是一件秘密的事情。

sentences.en: It was a secret thing, but a very, very open secret.
sentences.zh: 这是一件秘密的事情，但也是一个非常、非常公开的秘密。

sentences.en: These guys have been operating all over the world.
sentences.zh: 这些人一直在世界各地行动。

sentences.en: They've been operating in Libya and Syria.
sentences.zh: 他们曾在利比亚和叙利亚活动。

sentences.en: And basically what this is, it's a deniable arm of the Russian military.
sentences.zh: 基本上，这就是俄罗斯军队的一个可以被否认的分支。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: It operates semi-autonomously.
sentences.zh: 它半自主地运作。

sentences.en: As far as we know, based on our reporting, they make decisions on their own, but they are definitely a tool in the Kremlin's arsenal.
sentences.zh: 据我们所知，根据我们的报道，他们自己做决定，但他们绝对是克里姆林宫军火库中的一个工具。

sentences.en: They are pursuing the Kremlin's geopolitical goals, only they're deniable.
sentences.zh: 他们正在追求克里姆林宫的地缘政治目标，只是他们是可以被否认的。

sentences.en: So if Wagner is operating somewhere in Syria, gets into a little bit of trouble because of human rights violations, this has happened, in fact.
sentences.zh: 所以如果瓦格纳在叙利亚某处行动，因为侵犯人权而惹上了一点麻烦，事实上这种情况已经发生过。

sentences.en: The Kremlin can say they do nothing about it.
sentences.zh: 克里姆林宫可以说他们对此一无所知。

sentences.en: They don't know who these people are.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道这些人是谁。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: But the point is that these guys have real military experience.
sentences.zh: 但重点是这些人有真正的军事经验。

sentences.en: And that's not something you can say for the bulk of the Russian military.
sentences.zh: 而这并不是你可以对大多数俄罗斯军队所说的话。

sentences.en: The Russian military hasn't fought a war like this in decades.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯军队几十年来没有打过这样的战争。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: It looks like World War I, they're fighting over miles of territory, trench warfare, jockeying for position.
sentences.zh: 这看起来像第一次世界大战，他们在为几英里的领土而战，进行堑壕战，争夺阵地。

sentences.en: Nobody has this kind of experience.
sentences.zh: 没有人有这种经验。

sentences.en: Nobody but these Wagner troops.
sentences.zh: 除了这些瓦格纳部队，没人有。

sentences.en: Okay, so they go to this Wagner group, this catering guy, for experienced men mainly.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以他们去找这个瓦格纳集团，这个餐饮老板，主要是为了有经验的人。

sentences.en: But what happens then?
sentences.zh: 但接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: Like, what does he do?
sentences.zh: 他做了什么？

sentences.en: Well, Prigozhin's role is that he's bringing in these experienced guys, but Russia also needs bodies.
sentences.zh: 嗯，普里戈任的角色是他带来了这些有经验的人，但俄罗斯也需要兵源。

sentences.en: And Prigozhin comes up with what you might call a creative solution.
sentences.zh: 普里戈任想出了一个你可以称之为“创造性”的解决方案。

sentences.en: He starts recruiting men from prisons to send to the front lines.
sentences.zh: 他开始从监狱招募人员送往一线。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So that's a step.
sentences.zh: 那真是一步险棋。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then these videos start appearing of him going to these prisons and recruiting prisoners.
sentences.zh: 然后开始出现他去监狱招募囚犯的视频。

sentences.en: And he gives them this patriotic pitch.
sentences.zh: 他给他们灌输爱国主义那一套。

sentences.en: He's like, look, you guys screwed up.
sentences.zh: 他说，看，你们搞砸了。

sentences.en: You're in here.
sentences.zh: 你们被关在这里。

sentences.en: You're a drain on the state.
sentences.zh: 你们是国家的负担。

sentences.en: How's about you turn your life around and do something for the good of the country?
sentences.zh: 何不改过自新，为国家做点好事呢？

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: If you survive, we will pardon you.
sentences.zh: 如果你活下来，我们将赦免你。

sentences.en: You'll get a clean slate.
sentences.zh: 你会有一个清白的记录。

sentences.en: You'll be able to go back to your life and live a normal life back home if you survive.
sentences.zh: 如果你活下来，你将能够回到你的生活中，在家乡过上正常的生活。

sentences.en: If you don't survive, we're going to make sure that you're honored, that you're going to be buried in a hallowed place, that you're going to be awarded.
sentences.zh: 如果你没活下来，我们会确保你受到荣誉，你会葬在神圣的地方，你会获得奖章。

sentences.en: You're not going to be remembered as an inmate in a prison.
sentences.zh: 你不会被记住是一个监狱里的囚犯。

sentences.en: You're going to be remembered as a hero to Russia.
sentences.zh: 你会被记住是俄罗斯的英雄。

sentences.en: And do people sign up?
sentences.zh: 人们会报名吗？

sentences.en: Like, are people in prisons buying what Prigozhin is selling?
sentences.zh: 监狱里的人会买普里戈任的账吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, as far as we know, that hundreds of these inmates have taken Prigozhin up on this deal.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，据我们所知，成百上千的囚犯接受了普里戈任的这笔交易。

sentences.en: The problem is, is they're not always the most reliable soldiers.
sentences.zh: 问题是，他们并不总是最可靠的士兵。

sentences.en: I met with one of these prisoner soldiers by the name of Yevgeny Nuzhin.
sentences.zh: 我见过其中一名囚犯士兵，名叫叶夫根尼·努任。

sentences.en: This guy is 55 years old.
sentences.zh: 这家伙55岁了。

sentences.en: He's doing time for murder.
sentences.zh: 他因谋杀罪服刑。

sentences.en: He's been in prison for more than 20 years.
sentences.zh: 他在监狱里待了20多年了。

sentences.en: And Prigozhin comes to his prison in AuguSt.
sentences.zh: 普里戈任在8月来到他的监狱。

sentences.en: He's on the ground in Ukraine by September.
sentences.zh: 他在9月就到了乌克兰战场。

sentences.en: And his job, he says, basically, is to sit in a trench and by nightfall, go out into the field of battle and collect the bodies of dead Wagner soldiers.
sentences.zh: 他说，他的工作基本上就是坐在战壕里，天黑后走到战场上，收集瓦格纳阵亡士兵的尸体。

sentences.en: God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: This is his job.
sentences.zh: 这就是他的工作。

sentences.en: And it gives you a sense of the carnage that's happening out there.
sentences.zh: 这让你感觉到那里正在发生的杀戮有多惨烈。

sentences.en: But he doesn't stay.
sentences.zh: 但他没有留下来。

sentences.en: He doesn't stay.
sentences.zh: 他没有留下来。

sentences.en: And can you tell us, just, how did you get here?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我们，你是怎么到这儿来的吗？

sentences.en: Well, I just wanted to go here.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我只是想来这里。

sentences.en: I left.
sentences.zh: 我离开了。

sentences.en: His plan all along, he said, was to take this deal and escape.
sentences.zh: 他说，他一直以来的计划就是接受这笔交易然后逃跑。

sentences.en: And that's just what he did.
sentences.zh: 而他正是这么做的。

sentences.en: He left the position.
sentences.zh: 他离开了阵地。

sentences.en: He left the release and left the automatic position.
sentences.zh: 他离开了释放点，离开了自动阵地。

sentences.en: On his second day at the front, he was going to go out and do his job of collecting bodies.
sentences.zh: 在前线的第二天，他本该出去执行收集尸体的工作。

sentences.en: But instead, he wandered over the lines and came upon a very startled group of Ukrainian soldiers who knocked him unconscious and tied him up.
sentences.zh: 但相反，他走过了防线，撞见了一群非常吃惊的乌克兰士兵，他们把他打晕并绑了起来。

sentences.en: And when he woke up, he was in Ukrainian custody, which is where I met him in October.
sentences.zh: 当他醒来时，他已经在乌克兰的拘留所里了，也就是我在10月份见到他的地方。

sentences.en: And what did he tell you?
sentences.zh: 他跟你说了什么？

sentences.en: He was proud of what he had done.
sentences.zh: 他为自己所做的一切感到自豪。

sentences.en: And he told me that, what good has Putin done in the time that he's been in power?
sentences.zh: 他问我，普京执政期间到底做了什么好事？

sentences.en: Has he done anything good?
sentences.zh: 他做过什么好事吗？

sentences.en: He said he thinks that the war was going to be Putin's grave.
sentences.zh: 他说他认为这场战争会成为普京的坟墓。

sentences.en: And, you know, hundreds of Wagner troops have been killed.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，成百上千的瓦格纳部队士兵已经被杀了。

sentences.en: The vast majority, according to Ukraine's military intelligence, are these inmates who are simply sent to the front lines, as best we can tell, to serve as canter fodder,
sentences.zh: 据乌克兰军方情报显示，绝大多数人都是这些囚犯，据我们所知，他们被送往一线，充当炮灰，

sentences.en: to draw the bullets of Ukrainian forces and wear them down.
sentences.zh: 用来消耗乌克兰军队的弹药，拖垮他们。

sentences.en: Okay, so at the end of the day, the Wagner group is not turning the war around.
sentences.zh: 好吧，归根结底，瓦格纳集团并没有扭转战局。

sentences.en: And at the same time, it's horrible carnage at the place where these guys are ending up.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，这些家伙最终落得的下场简直是惨绝人寰。

sentences.en: So you kind of can imagine why someone like Yevgeny, the guy you talked to, decided to flee, right?
sentences.zh: 所以你可以想象为什么像叶夫根尼这样的人，也就是你采访的那个人，决定逃跑，对吧？

sentences.en: So, Mike, what happened to Yevgeny?
sentences.zh: 那么，迈克，叶夫根尼后来怎么样了？

sentences.en: Well, when Yevgeny took this deal, Prigozhin issued a warning.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当叶夫根尼接受了这笔交易时，普里戈任发出了警告。

sentences.en: He said that any of these inmates who decided to go along to Ukraine and fight for Russia and Ukraine, if it were found out that they deserted, that they turned themselves in,
sentences.zh: 他说，任何决定去乌克兰为俄罗斯而战的囚犯，如果被发现逃兵，或者投降，

sentences.en: that they ran from the battlefield, there would be severe consequences.
sentences.zh: 如果他们从战场上逃跑，后果将非常严重。

sentences.en: He said in one of his videos that they would be shot.
sentences.zh: 他在一段视频中说，他们会被枪决。

sentences.en: And somehow, after we spoke, Yevgeny ended up back into the hands of Wagner fighters.
sentences.zh: 不知何故，在我们谈话后，叶夫根尼又落回了瓦格纳战士的手中。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: He was traded?
sentences.zh: 他被交换了？

sentences.en: Yes, it was as a result of a prisoner swap.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是战俘交换的结果。

sentences.en: The Ukrainians gave him back to the Russians.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰人把他交还给了俄罗斯人。

sentences.en: And the next time I saw him was in a video that appeared online.
sentences.zh: 我再次见到他是在网上出现的一段视频里。

sentences.en: And Yevgeny's head was taped to a block.
sentences.zh: 叶夫根尼的头被胶带固定在砖块上。

sentences.en: And standing over him was this man in camouflage holding a sledgehammer.
sentences.zh: 站在他上方的是一个穿着迷彩服、拿着大锤的男人。

sentences.en: And in this video, Yevgeny speaks.
sentences.zh: 在视频中，叶夫根尼开口说话了。

sentences.en: He said he woke up in a basement and was told that he was going to be judged.
sentences.zh: 他说他在地下室醒来，被告知他将接受审判。

sentences.en: And when he says that, the man with the sledgehammer swings it down and crushes his skull.
sentences.zh: 当他说完这些话时，那个拿大锤的男人挥下大锤，砸碎了他的头骨。

sentences.en: Oh, my God, Mike.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪，迈克。

sentences.en: It's like an ISIS beheading video.
sentences.zh: 这就像伊斯兰国的斩首视频一样。

sentences.en: It's very similar to that.
sentences.zh: 非常相似。

sentences.en: And if there was any doubt about how Prigozhin felt about it, he released a statement endorsing Yevgeny's murder.
sentences.zh: 如果有人对普里戈任对此事的态度有任何怀疑，他发表了一份声明，支持对叶夫根尼的谋杀。

sentences.en: He said Yevgeny betrayed his people, betrayed his comrades, betrayed them consciously.
sentences.zh: 他说叶夫根尼背叛了他的同胞，背叛了他的战友，是有意识地背叛了他们。

sentences.en: He planned his escape.
sentences.zh: 他策划了自己的逃跑。

sentences.en: Nuzhin is a traitor.
sentences.zh: 努任是个叛徒。

sentences.en: That's a statement that he put out shortly after the execution was carried out.
sentences.zh: 这是他在处决执行后不久发表的声明。

sentences.en: And what I think is happening here is that this is something like a trial balloon.
sentences.zh: 我认为这里发生的事情就像是一个试探性的气球。

sentences.en: Russia is in danger in Ukraine, and it needs solutions.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯在乌克兰处于危险之中，需要解决方案。

sentences.en: And Prigozhin has been brought in to find solutions.
sentences.zh: 普里戈任被请来寻找解决方案。

sentences.en: And he's come up with this extreme solution.
sentences.zh: 他提出了这个极端的方案。

sentences.en: This level of terror, of keeping control and keeping order among the ranks of Russian soldiers in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 这种恐怖手段，是为了在乌克兰的俄罗斯士兵队伍中保持控制和秩序。

sentences.en: It's not clear whether this type of treatment will be expanded to the rest of the Russian military.
sentences.zh: 目前还不清楚这种对待方式是否会扩大到俄罗斯军队的其他部分。

sentences.en: But this is the Kremlin struggling to come up with answers for how to right the ship in Ukraine and start making some gains.
sentences.zh: 但这反映了克里姆林宫在努力寻找如何扭转乌克兰局势并开始取得进展的答案。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《Dealbook》报道商业和政策。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的Dealbook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最有影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、佐兰·蒙达尼等等。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日通过nytimes.com直播部分采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download The New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: So, Mike, you've brought us to early fall.
sentences.zh: 那么，迈克，你把我们带到了初秋。

sentences.en: The Russian military has failed to live up to their own expectations over and over.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯军队一次又一次地未能达到他们自己的期望。

sentences.en: They're casting about with their Plan Bs and Plan Cs, losing tons of their own men, and beginning to use brutal tactics to keep them in line.
sentences.zh: 他们四处寻找B计划和C计划，损失了大量自己的人，并开始使用残酷的手段来维持纪律。

sentences.en: And we know that by September, Putin announces a draft to get even more men.
sentences.zh: 我们知道到9月份，普京宣布征兵以获得更多的人力。

sentences.en: So what happens inside the Russian military at this point?
sentences.zh: 那么此时俄罗斯军队内部发生了什么？

sentences.en: What effect does that have?
sentences.zh: 这产生了什么影响？

sentences.en: Well, the one major effect that it has is that it takes about 250,000, 300,000 Russian men who, for the first five, six months of this war, had been watching it from the sidelines,
sentences.zh: 嗯，它产生的一个主要影响是，它带走了大约25万到30万名俄罗斯男性，他们在战争的前五六个月里一直是在场边观望，

sentences.en: essentially watching it on their couch, watching it on Russian television,
sentences.zh: 基本上是在沙发上看着，在俄罗斯电视上看着，

sentences.en: and throws them onto the front lines with barely any training and really little sense of what they were supposed to be doing.
sentences.zh: 然后把他们扔到前线，几乎没有任何训练，对他们应该做什么也知之甚少。

sentences.en: I was able to contact several troops from Russia's 155th Naval Infantry Brigade, which is a unit based in Russia's far, far east,
sentences.zh: 我联系到了俄罗斯第155海军步兵旅的几名士兵，这是一个驻扎在俄罗斯极东地区的部队，

sentences.en: so about as far from Ukraine as you can possibly get and still be in Russia.
sentences.zh: 离乌克兰尽可能远，但仍然在俄罗斯境内。

sentences.en: I spoke to them weeks after they had been drafted, and they described a scene of utter horror and chaos.
sentences.zh: 我在他们被征召几周后采访了他们，他们描述了一个极其恐怖和混乱的场景。

sentences.en: They entered the battlefield bumbling through these cratered farms in these fields with no maps, no working medical kits or walkie-talkies,
sentences.zh: 他们进入战场，在这些布满弹坑的农场和田野里跌跌撞撞，没有地图，没有有效的医疗包或对讲机，

sentences.en: no ability to communicate with one another.
sentences.zh: 无法相互沟通。

sentences.en: One platoon medic was a former barista who had never had any medical training.
sentences.zh: 一名排级医务兵以前是个咖啡师，从未接受过任何医疗培训。

sentences.en: And they were ordered forward going through these fields with these Kalashnikov rifles that were made in the 1960s and virtually nothing to eat.
sentences.zh: 他们被命令向前推进，拿着20世纪60年代制造的卡拉什尼科夫步枪，几乎没有吃的。

sentences.en: Some of them had never fired a gun before, and those that had hadn't done so since they were 18-year-old conscripts.
sentences.zh: 有些人以前从未开过枪，而那些开过枪的人自18岁应征入伍以来就没再碰过枪。

sentences.en: They had no artillery.
sentences.zh: 他们没有炮火支援。

sentences.en: They had no air cover.
sentences.zh: 他们没有空中掩护。

sentences.en: They had very little ammunition.
sentences.zh: 他们的弹药非常匮乏。

sentences.en: But when they were describing this, they said they weren't frightened by any of these conditions initially because they were promised by their commanders
sentences.zh: 但当他们描述这些时，他们说起初并没有被这些条件吓倒，因为他们的指挥官向他们承诺，

sentences.en: that they'd never seek combat.
sentences.zh: 他们永远不会参加战斗。

sentences.en: And it was only when Ukrainian shells began crashing on their heads and ripping their comrades to pieces did they realize that they had been duped.
sentences.zh: 直到乌克兰的炮弹开始在他们头上爆炸，把他们的战友炸得粉碎时，他们才意识到自己被骗了。

sentences.en: And I spoke to members of a single platoon.
sentences.zh: 我采访了一个排的成员。

sentences.en: They went in with 60 men on a march in a single day.
sentences.zh: 他们一天之内行军投入了60人。

sentences.en: Forty of them were killed.
sentences.zh: 其中40人被杀。

sentences.en: God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: In a single four-hour stretch in eastern Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 在乌克兰东部短短四个小时的时间里。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I mean, that is truly cannon fodder.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那真是炮灰。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, it's like the Russian military is not learning at all.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，俄罗斯军队似乎根本没有吸取教训。

sentences.en: Like, it's just failure after failure.
sentences.zh: 就像是一次又一次的失败。

sentences.en: And you'd think at some point they'd recalibrate.
sentences.zh: 你以为他们会在某个时候进行调整。

sentences.en: But they aren't.
sentences.zh: 但他们没有。

sentences.en: Like, they'd just keep going with this throw bodies at this problem and have them destroyed.
sentences.zh: 他们只是继续用人命去填补这个问题，让他们被摧毁。

sentences.en: And that's the problem that we identified at the very beginning of the war.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在战争初期发现的问题。

sentences.en: And these problems have persisted throughout.
sentences.zh: 这些问题一直持续到现在。

sentences.en: And the soldiers that I talked to from the 155th, they understood that intrinsically.
sentences.zh: 我采访的第155旅的士兵们，他们本质上理解这一点。

sentences.en: I spoke to one of the survivors, a Russian soldier named Alexander.
sentences.zh: 我采访了幸存者之一，一名叫亚历山大的俄罗斯士兵。

sentences.en: He recovered in a military hospital in the south of Russia.
sentences.zh: 他在俄罗斯南部的一家军事医院康复。

sentences.en: And what he said is, you know, when he looked out over the battlefield, all he saw were legs and guts and meat.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，当他望向战场时，他看到的只有断肢、内脏和血肉。

sentences.en: He said,
sentences.zh: 他说，

sentences.en: I know it sounds terrible, but you can't describe it any other way.
sentences.zh: 我知道这听起来很可怕，但你无法用其他方式来描述它。

sentences.en: People were turned into hamburger.
sentences.zh: 人们变成了肉泥。

sentences.en: God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: And Mike, what was his feeling after all of this?
sentences.zh: 迈克，经历这一切后，他的感受是什么？

sentences.en: Like, you were talking to him from a military hospital after, of course, he'd already been wounded and made it back to Russia.
sentences.zh: 你是从军事医院采访他的，当然，他已经受伤并回到了俄罗斯。

sentences.en: Like, was he angry at the Russian military?
sentences.zh: 他是否对俄罗斯军队感到愤怒？

sentences.en: Like, at his commanders?
sentences.zh: 对他的指挥官感到愤怒吗？

sentences.en: I mean, the thing that enraged him most were the lies.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，最让他愤怒的是谎言。

sentences.en: He was lied to by the Russian media, which told him from his couch in far eastern Russia when he was watching this war in its early months
sentences.zh: 他被俄罗斯媒体欺骗了，当他在俄罗斯远东的沙发上观看战争初期时，媒体告诉他

sentences.en: that everything was going according to plan, that everything is going well.
sentences.zh: 一切都在按计划进行，一切都很顺利。

sentences.en: He was lied to by his commanders, who said that he was only going to be involved in a support role and wouldn't be on the front lines.
sentences.zh: 他被指挥官欺骗了，指挥官说他只会担任支援角色，不会在前线。

sentences.en: These were people who were utterly unequipped to be sent into war, and yet they were sent into war anyway.
sentences.zh: 这些人根本没有装备去参战，但还是被送上了战场。

sentences.en: Alexander told me that he was drafted in September along with three of his close childhood friends.
sentences.zh: 亚历山大告诉我，他和三个童年好友在9月份被征召入伍。

sentences.en: He was in the hospital from a severe concussion from the shelling that his unit had come under.
sentences.zh: 他因为部队遭受炮击而受到严重脑震荡，住进了医院。

sentences.en: Another one of these four friends that suffered similar injuries was in the hospital for a concussion.
sentences.zh: 这四个朋友中的另一个也遭受了类似的伤害，因脑震荡住院。

sentences.en: One lost both legs, and the fourth is missing.
sentences.zh: 一个失去了双腿，第四个失踪了。

sentences.en: Oh, that is devastating.
sentences.zh: 噢，那太令人心碎了。

sentences.en: And just complete disregard for human life.
sentences.zh: 完全无视人的生命。

sentences.en: Right, but what he told me is that he fully expects to be discharged from the hospital, given that his injuries are light, and that when he does, he'll be going back to Ukraine,
sentences.zh: 没错，但他告诉我，他完全预计出院后会回到乌克兰，因为他的伤势较轻，而且他会自愿回去。

sentences.en: and that he's going to be doing so willingly.
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 他可能反对战争的进行方式，但他并不反对战争本身。

sentences.en: He may be opposed to how the war is being conducted, but he's not opposed to the war.
sentences.zh: 但是迈克，经历了这一切，失去了朋友，看到了那些景象，他为什么要回去？

sentences.en: But why would he go back, Mike, after all of this, the loss of his friends, what he saw?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Like, why?
sentences.zh: 你知道，关于亚历山大，我发现最令人着迷的是，他明白俄罗斯士兵在地面上被当作垃圾对待。

sentences.en: You know, the thing that I found most fascinating about Alexander is he understood that the Russian soldiers on the ground are being treated like crap.
sentences.zh: 他明白战争进行得很糟糕，尽管俄罗斯的宣传告诉他并非如此。

sentences.en: He understood that the war is going poorly, despite what the Russian propaganda is telling him.
sentences.zh: 但他最终的结论是，他对此无能为力。

sentences.en: But his ultimate conclusion is that there's nothing he can do about it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是他的命。

sentences.en: You know, that this is his lot in life.
sentences.zh: 当你采访很多这些士兵时，你会遇到这种矛盾的宿命论。

sentences.en: It's this sort of ambivalent fatalism that you meet when you talk to a lot of these soldiers.
sentences.zh: 他在谈话中告诉我，这就是我们的成长方式。

sentences.en: He told me in our conversation, this is how we were raised.
sentences.zh: 我们在自己的国家长大，明白国家如何对待我们并不重要。

sentences.en: We grew up in our country, understanding that it doesn't matter how our country treats us.
sentences.zh: 也许这很糟糕。

sentences.en: Maybe this is bad.
sentences.zh: 也许这很好。

sentences.en: Maybe this is good.
sentences.zh: 也许我们不喜欢政府的某些方面。

sentences.en: Maybe there are things that we do not like about our government.
sentences.zh: 但他补充说，

sentences.en: But he added,
sentences.zh: 当这种情况出现时，我们就会起身出发。

sentences.en: when a situation like this arises, we get up and go.
sentences.zh: 这是俄罗斯永恒的谜团。

sentences.en: It is the eternal mystery of Russia.

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 但是如果你可以免费探索《时报》一个月，而无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序，首月即可免费使用。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《纽约时报》订阅用户每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果您尚未订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载时报应用程序，即可获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是您今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: Madam Clerk, on behalf of the House Republican Conference, I rise today to nominate the gentleman from California,
sentences.zh: 书记官女士，我谨代表众议院共和党党团，提名来自加利福尼亚州的议员，

sentences.en: Kevin McCarthy, as Speaker of the House to lead America's new Republican majority.
sentences.zh: 凯文·麦卡锡，担任众议院议长，领导美国新的共和党多数派。

sentences.en: In a dramatic revolt against their own leader, a group of hard-right Republicans rejected Representative Kevin McCarthy as the next Speaker of the House
sentences.zh: 在一场针对本党领袖的戏剧性反叛中，一群极右翼共和党人拒绝支持众议员凯文·麦卡锡出任下一任众议院议长，

sentences.en: in three different rounds of voting, denying him the 218 votes that he needed.
sentences.zh: 在三轮投票中，他未能获得所需的218票。

sentences.en: No persons having received a majority of the whole number of votes cast by surname, a Speaker has not been elected.
sentences.zh: 由于无人获得过半数投票，议长尚未选出。

sentences.en: It was a humiliating setback for McCarthy, who has struggled to persuade right-wing lawmakers to trust him.
sentences.zh: 这对麦卡锡来说是一个羞辱性的挫折，他一直难以说服右翼议员信任他。

sentences.en: McCarthy could only afford to lose the votes of four Republican colleagues.
sentences.zh: 麦卡锡最多只能承受四名共和党同僚的倒戈。

sentences.en: Instead, he lost as many as 20.
sentences.zh: 然而，他却失去了多达20人的支持。

sentences.en: After the third round of voting, the House adjourned without having chosen a leader, something that has not happened in nearly 100 years.
sentences.zh: 在第三轮投票后，众议院在未选出领袖的情况下休会，这种情况在近100年来尚属首次。

sentences.en: Following the procedure used by the House in 1923, the clerk is prepared to direct the reading clerk to call a roll anew.
sentences.zh: 按照众议院1923年使用的程序，书记官准备指示宣读书记官重新进行点名投票。

sentences.en: Under House rules, voting for Speaker will resume later today and will continue until a Speaker is elected.
sentences.zh: 根据众议院规则，议长选举将于今天晚些时候恢复，并将持续进行，直到选出议长为止。

sentences.en: And,
sentences.zh: 此外，

sentences.en: Damar Hamlin, the Buffalo Bills defensive back, remained in critical condition on Tuesday after he went into cardiac arrest following a routine tackle during a primetime NFL game.
sentences.zh: 布法罗比尔队的防守后卫达马尔·哈姆林周二仍处于危急状态。此前，他在一场NFL黄金时段比赛中进行常规擒抱后心脏骤停。

sentences.en: In a highly unusual decision, the NFL suspended the game after Hamlin collapsed on the field.
sentences.zh: NFL做出了一个极不寻常的决定，在哈姆林倒地后暂停了比赛。

sentences.en: It was the latest incident to raise questions about player safety in professional football.
sentences.zh: 这是最新一起引发人们对职业橄榄球球员安全问题的质疑事件。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Claire Tannes-Sketter and Luke van der Broek.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由克莱尔·坦内斯-斯凯特和卢克·范德布鲁克制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Mark George and Lisa Chow with help from Paige Cowett.
sentences.zh: 由马克·乔治和丽莎·周编辑，佩奇·考伊特提供了协助。

sentences.en: Contains translations by Anastasia Varashtsova.
sentences.zh: 包含安娜斯塔西娅·瓦拉什托娃的翻译。

sentences.en: Original music by Rowan Nemisto and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 原创音乐由罗文·内米斯托创作，克里斯·伍德负责工程处理。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Lansford of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly乐队的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯福德创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西。

sentences.en: We'll see you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我们明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine until this summer.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作，直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场激烈、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在我和莎拉·凯尼格主持的最新一期《地铁》节目中，我们将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《地铁》节目。

sentences.zh: 让我们开始吧。
